findings.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the raw Zod safeParse wrapper ({success, data}) while this call site persists that wrapper directly as credential.key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse() which returned the parsed data. On the first token refresh (default, non-sharing mode), prisma stores {success:true, data:{...}} as the Google credential key; the next time the credential is loaded, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails because access_token/refresh_token now live one level down, so every Google Calendar availability check and booking throws until the user re-connects — stored credentials are corrupted.

[BUG] When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data expecting the gaxios token body that myGoogleAuth.refreshToken previously returned. A fetch Response has no .data property, so token is undefined and token.access_token on line 95 throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined — the Google Calendar refresh path crashes on every credential-sync-enabled instance instead of fetching tokens.

[BUG] The computed schema keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the single literal property name "[object Object]" (ZodString defines no toString override), so minimumTokenResponseSchema validates only access_token while Zod's default strip mode discards every other response field, after which line 26 writes the literal string "refresh_token" into the parsed data. In credential-sharing mode every caller persists credentials reduced to {access_token, refresh_token:"refresh_token"} — Zoom and Office365 spread that literal over their stored key, and Salesforce stores a two-field key that drops instance_url, so the next service construction reads undefined instance_url/refresh_token; if the operator later disables sharing, refresh requests send the literal "refresh_token" and those integrations are permanently bricked.

[BUG] The route default-imports zod (import z from "zod"), but zod's CommonJS entry sets __esModule and exports no default, so z binds to undefined at runtime. z.object(...) on line 9 throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'object') when the route module first loads, so every request to POST /api/webhook/app-credential returns a 500 — the inbound credential-sync webhook never functions at all (every other file in this repo uses import { z } from "zod").

[BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but line 217 evaluates zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error expecting the axios response shape the wrapped function returns. Response.data is undefined, so if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error') — every Zoho CRM calendar operation crashes whenever credential sharing is enabled.

[BUG] In sharing mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but line 95 evaluates tokenInfo.data.error expecting the axios response shape. Response.data is undefined, so if (!tokenInfo.data.error) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error') — every Zoho Bigin calendar operation crashes whenever credential sharing is enabled.

[BUG] The HubSpot refresh assigns refreshOAuthTokens' raw fetch Response to a HubspotToken, and the unchanged downstream code reads access_token/expires_in/refresh_token off that Response. In credential-sharing mode hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in and access_token are undefined, so the credential is persisted with a NaN expiry_date and the HubSpot client is handed an undefined access token — every HubSpot-integrated booking fails while sharing is enabled.

[BUG] The zoho-bigin call passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter (used verbatim as calcomUserId in the sync request body), while all other call sites pass credential.userId. The parent sync endpoint receives the credential row's id labeled as the Cal.com user id, cannot map it to a user, and zoho-bigin token sync fails while every other integrated app syncs correctly.

[ADVISORY] The Salesforce service now performs an unconditional token-refresh POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction, where the jsforce connection previously refreshed lazily only when the stored access token was rejected. Every availability check and booking against a Salesforce credential now pays an extra OAuth round-trip and a credential DB write (Salesforce token endpoints are rate-limited), and a transient refresh failure that previously only affected an expired token now aborts all Salesforce operations whose stored token was still valid.

[ADVISORY] The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug — no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, no header, no signature — even though the inbound webhook authenticates callers with exactly that secret. The parent application cannot verify the request came from its Cal.com instance, so anyone able to reach the endpoint URL can request current OAuth access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user ids — self-hosters exposing the endpoint hand out their users' tokens.

[ADVISORY] The webhook has no error handling around symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse (and none around the zod parse at line 31), and it persists the decrypted object to credential.key without any schema validation. A malformed body or a payload encrypted with a different key throws unhandled and the caller gets a 500 instead of a 4xx; worse, a wrongly-shaped but decryptable payload is stored verbatim, so the next booking that loads the credential fails inside googleCredentialSchema.parse et al. and the poison credential must be deleted from the database manually.

[ADVISORY] The office365video refresh passes appSlug "msteams", which is not the app's store slug (office365video), while every other call site in this diff passes the app's real slug (google-calendar, hubspot, zoomvideo, webex, zoho-bigin, zohocrm, lark-calendar, office365-calendar). A parent app that keys its sync endpoint on Cal.com app slugs — as the webhook's own app lookup and the other eight call sites imply — cannot resolve "msteams", so MS Teams token sync fails while all other apps sync, silently degrading the Teams integration on credential-sync instances.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds an authenticated webhook handler, an env-forked refresh dispatcher used by eight apps, and a response-parsing helper, none of which is covered by any test in the diff. The persist-then-reload contract between parseRefreshTokenResponse and its callers is exactly what the Google wrapper-persistence bug in this diff breaks, and nothing in the suite would catch that class of regression — enabling credential sharing or changing any refresh path reaches users with zero test signal.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full ZodSafeParseResult wrapper ({success, data}) but Google Calendar stores that wrapper directly as the credential `key` (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the parsed data). On every deployment (sync enabled or not), the first Google Calendar token refresh overwrites credential.key with {success:true, data:{...}}; on the next refresh cycle googleCredentials.refresh_token is undefined, myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(undefined) fails, and all Google Calendar availability/booking operations throw — the real refresh_token is buried in wrapper.data and every user must reconnect the app.

[BUG] The sync branch returns the raw fetch Response object without calling .json(), while several wired adapters expect library-shaped return values (google-auth-library's res, axios's AxiosResponse, hubspot's parsed HubspotToken). With sync enabled, GoogleCalendarService gets res?.data === undefined and throws TypeError on token.access_token (CalendarService.ts:93-94), zoho-bigin and zohocrm throw TypeError reading tokenInfo.data.error, Hubspot stores undefined tokens with a NaN expiry, and lark's handleLarkError rejects the parent's flat {access_token, expiry} envelope — bookings against these apps fail in sync mode no matter what the operator's endpoint returns.

[BUG] The sync-mode gate omits the userId check that refreshOAuthTokens applies, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is used whenever the env flags are set even when the token was refreshed natively (Salesforce never routes through refreshOAuthTokens at all). On sync-enabled deployments Salesforce refreshes against login.salesforce.com then stores a key stripped to {access_token, refresh_token} — instance_url, signature, scope and token_type are dropped (z.object strips unknown keys), so the next jsforce.Connection is built without an instance URL and Salesforce breaks permanently; team-owned (userId null) Office365 credentials likewise get their rotated refresh_token overwritten with the literal "refresh_token".

[BUG] Both computed schema keys, [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], evaluate to the literal property name "[object Object]" (the second silently overwrites the first), so the "any number property is the expiry" catch-all described in the comment does not exist and z.object strips every real field except access_token. In sync mode no expiry field (expiry_date/expires_in) is ever validated or preserved: Office365 credentials keep their stale expired expiry_date and hit the parent sync endpoint on every calendar operation, and Zoom credentials lose expires_in entirely, forcing a refresh per call.

[BUG] The service passes credentialId (the credential row id) as refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter, which is documented and used as the cal.com user id in the sync request body. With sync enabled, the parent endpoint receives the credential's DB id as calcomUserId — it either fails to resolve a user or returns a different user's OAuth tokens, which are then stored under this credential, cross-linking another user's integration access or breaking Zoho Bigin sync entirely.

[BUG] The outbound fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication (no shared secret, no auth header), while the inbound webhook direction enforces CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The operator's token-issuing endpoint has no shipped way to authenticate Cal.com's calls — anyone who learns the endpoint URL can request live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary cal.com user ids, defeating the secret-based trust model the feature itself establishes.

[BUG] The handler performs no req.method check and calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no try/catch, so schema, decryption and JSON errors propagate unhandled. A GET request, or a correctly-secreted but malformed payload (missing body, non-JSON ciphertext, non-32-byte encryption key), returns a bare 500 instead of the 400/405 a webhook contract needs, leaving the integrating operator with no diagnosable error from their own misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap: the diff ships a new externally-callable webhook (secret auth, AES decryption, credential upsert), two new utilities, and rewired token-refresh/persistence across ten integrations with zero test files — a scan of the diff finds none under any test path or test-name pattern. Regressions like the parse→safeParse wrapper change that corrupts Google credential keys pass straight to production because no assertion anywhere in the diff covers a token-refresh round trip or the webhook's auth/decrypt/upsert behavior.

[ADVISORY] The constructor path now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a credential DB write on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, replacing jsforce's previous lazy on-demand refresh. Every Salesforce-connected booking or availability check incurs a round trip to login.salesforce.com and a credential row update even when the stored token is minutes old, multiplying Salesforce API usage, latency, and DB write load on the hot booking path.

[ADVISORY] The sync gate requires a non-null userId, silently excluding team-owned credentials (userId null) from credential sync with no error, log, or documentation of the exclusion, while the webhook schema equally only accepts a user id. Self-hosters running the sync model do not configure their own OAuth client secrets (the parent app owns them), so team-connected apps fall back to native refresh with missing client credentials and team bookings fail opaquely while per-user bookings keep working.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint JSON.parses and persists whatever the parent sends without validating the decrypted payload against the target app's credential schema, even though every refresh path in this same diff enforces zod schemas on the same key field. A parent app pushing a structurally wrong payload (missing access_token, wrong field names, or even a non-object JSON value) receives a 200, and the end user's bookings crash later inside the calendar service with errors that give no hint the webhook seeded the bad credential.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) and this code persists that envelope directly as the credential key, replacing the flat credential object that googleCredentialSchema.parse() previously returned. The first Google Calendar token refresh after this deploys writes {success:true, data:{...}} into Credential.key, so every subsequent GoogleCalendarService construction reads credential.key.access_token and credential.key.refresh_token as undefined and all Google Calendar operations fail for every user on every deployment, credential sharing enabled or not.

[BUG] When credential sharing is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint's raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data expecting the gaxios response shape and then dereferences token.access_token unguarded. With the feature enabled, res.data is undefined on a fetch Response and token.access_token throws a TypeError inside every Google Calendar token refresh, so Google Calendar fails exactly in the configuration this PR exists to enable.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint's raw fetch Response to seven call sites that each expect an app-native shape (gaxios .data, axios .data, HubSpot SDK token object) with no adaptation layer anywhere. The moment sync is enabled zoho-bigin (tokenInfo.data.error) and zohocrm (zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) throw TypeError reading 'error' of undefined because a fetch Response has no .data, hubspot receives a Response typed as HubspotToken so its expires_in arithmetic yields a NaN expiry, and lark/webex/zoom/office365/msteams receive response bodies their handlers never parse — the feature breaks every integration it was written to cover.

[BUG] This call passes credentialId (the credential row primary key) as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, which is serialized to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. When sync is enabled the parent application receives a credential id where the contract (and every sibling call site, which passes credential.userId) says Cal.com user id, so zoho-bigin token sync matches no user — or the wrong user where the ids numerically collide — and zoho-bigin credentials silently never refresh.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites the parsed data's refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token' whenever the response lacks one, and callers persist that data as the stored credential key. The sync response by design contains only access_token and expiry, so with sharing enabled the zoom/salesforce/office365 credential updates write the literal 'refresh_token' over the user's real refresh token, destroying the only material that can re-authorize; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset or the flag reverted, those integrations are permanently broken until each user manually reconnects the app.

[BUG] The spread ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) merges parseRefreshTokenResponse's sync-mode output — only {access_token} plus the injected literal refresh_token:'refresh_token' — into the office365 credential that is then written to the database. Enabling credential sharing on a deployment with Office365 calendars replaces each user's stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token' on the first refresh, so the credential can never be refreshed locally again and the user must reconnect the app.

[BUG] The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to identical literal stringified-schema property names, so minimumTokenResponseSchema implements none of its commented intent ('any property with a number is the expiry') and enforces nothing beyond access_token — no expiry property is ever validated. In sync mode a token response missing the expiry field parses successfully, so expiry_date/expires_in are never updated and office365/google credentials fail expiry checks or re-refresh on every operation, while the strict per-app schemas (googleCredentialSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) are silently discarded whenever the flag is on.

[ADVISORY] This PR adds an ungated Salesforce token refresh — a POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update — that executes on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens, and is not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED unlike every other behavior change in the diff. Every Salesforce calendar operation on every deployment (including ones that will never use credential sharing) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip and a DB write per service construction, and the response.statusText !== 'OK' gate converts any proxy that strips the reason phrase or any Salesforce error body into a thrown HttpError that kills the operation — a scope expansion traceable to no stated requirement.

[BUG] Salesforce's new refresh path never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so even with credential sharing enabled a Salesforce credential delivered by the app-credential webhook (refresh token issued to the parent app's OAuth client) is refreshed locally with this instance's consumer_key/consumer_secret. Salesforce rejects the mismatched client with invalid_grant, the statusText check throws HttpError 400, and the Salesforce integration is broken in exactly the configuration this PR exists to enable — the invariant 'shared credentials refresh via the sync endpoint' holds for nine apps and is violated for the tenth.

[BUG] The outbound sync request POSTs only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication of any kind — no shared secret, signature, or auth header, and no way for the operator to add one — even though the inbound webhook direction shipped in the same PR requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can enumerate sequential calcomUserIds against the public app-slug list and harvest live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users of the Cal.com deployment, because the parent app has no Cal.com-presented credential to verify and the hard-coded body leaves no place to put one.

[BUG] The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with no HTTP method guard and no error handling, and the later JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is equally unprotected. A GET request, a POST with a malformed body, or a keys value encrypted under a different key throws an unhandled ZodError or decryption error and returns a 500 instead of the 403/404 the endpoint's own convention promises, so the parent application cannot distinguish a contract violation from a Cal.com outage.

[ADVISORY] The redirect URI is rewritten from the config-driven `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` to the hardcoded literal 'zoho-bigin', a change unrelated to credential sync that nothing in the PR's stated intent explains. The install URL is silently decoupled from config.json, so any future slug or routing change leaves zoho-bigin OAuth installs failing with a redirect_uri mismatch, and a reviewer cannot trace this line to any requirement in this PR.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so its runtime value is the raw AES-256 encryption key string (or empty string), not a boolean. Any log line, error report, or serialized config that includes this exported flag prints the key that decrypts every synced app credential, and consumers that compare === true or persist the value get the secret itself instead of an on/off flag.

[ADVISORY] Replacing refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse plus the explicit console.error of the zodError and the Microsoft response with parseRefreshTokenResponse deletes the only diagnostics on this refresh path and substitutes a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' throw. Operators debugging the notoriously flaky Office365 token refresh now get no provider response payload and no zod detail in the logs, turning a previously diagnosable failure into an opaque error with no actionable fields.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's two computed keys both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (z.string().toString() on a Zod schema instance returns Object.prototype.toString's output, and the second computed key overwrites the first), so the sync-mode schema is really z.object({access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional()}) which validates only access_token and strips every other property — the opposite of the commented intent "Allow other properties in the token response". On any host with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every sync-mode parse returns only {access_token}: GoogleCalendarService.ts:96 persists that as the entire credential.key (destroying refresh_token and expiry_date), Office365CalendarService.ts:263 merges it so expiry_date is never updated (stale expiry forces a parent round-trip on every operation), and the app-specific schemas (zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) become dead code, so any parent response with a string access_token is accepted no matter what else it contains or lacks.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token whenever the sync-mode schema is selected (a schema that by construction can never produce a real refresh token), and every caller persists that sentinel into credential.key. Zoom (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts merges {...credential.key, ...parsedToken.data}) and Office365 (CalendarService.ts:263 merge) overwrite the user's real provider refresh_token with the string "refresh_token", and Google stores it wholesale; the moment CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is removed, or for team-owned credentials where userId is null (refreshOAuthTokens takes the local-refresh path at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 while parsing still uses the sync schema because its condition omits userId), the stored fake token is used against the provider and the credential is permanently bricked — every affected user must re-authenticate every app.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15), but this code reads res?.data — the googleapis Gaxios response shape — which is undefined on a fetch Response, so token.access_token throws a TypeError. google-calendar token refresh never succeeds on sync-enabled hosts: the TypeError hits the surrounding try/catch, the credential is never updated, and the service proceeds with an expired access token, so every calendar operation for that user fails with Google 401s — the flagship app of this PR cannot work with the feature the PR implements.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code assigns it to hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken and the following code reads .expires_in/.access_token directly off it — properties a fetch Response does not have. hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in is undefined so the expiry is computed as NaN and hubspotCredentialSchema.parse throws on the Response object (which lacks every HubspotToken field), so HubSpot token refresh always fails whenever sync is enabled and HubSpot operations requiring a fresh token break.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the very next statement reads tokenInfo.data — the axios response shape — which is undefined on a fetch Response, so !tokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes on every attempt when sync is enabled; the Bigin credential is never refreshed and the CRM integration fails for sync-enabled hosts.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the next statement reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data — the axios response shape — which is undefined on a fetch Response, so !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho CRM token refresh crashes on every attempt when sync is enabled; the credential is never refreshed and the Zoho CRM integration fails for sync-enabled hosts.

[BUG] BiginCalendarService passes credentialId (the Credential row's primary key, credential.id) as refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter named userId, where every other call site in this diff passes credential.userId. In sync mode the parent app receives calcomUserId=<credential id> — a value from the unrelated Credential id sequence — and either finds no user or returns the tokens of whichever user happens to own that id, so Bigin stores and operates on another user's Zoho credentials (cross-user CRM data corruption); the wrong binding is invisible because non-sync mode ignores the argument entirely.

[BUG] SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction — no expiry/isExpired guard, and no routing through refreshOAuthTokens — creating a parallel refresh path that duplicates jsforce's own OAuth refresh and bypasses the sync abstraction every other app in this PR uses. Every availability check and booking involving a Salesforce-connected user now makes a login.salesforce.com round trip (which counts against the org's Salesforce API/login limits) plus a DB write, even on hosts that never enable credential sharing: hot-path latency and org API-quota exhaustion are added to all Salesforce booking flows, and concurrent constructions race read-modify-write on credential.key.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse selects the sync-mode minimumTokenResponseSchema based on global env vars even though Salesforce obtains its response directly from login.salesforce.com (it never routes through the sync endpoint), so on sync-enabled hosts accessTokenParsed.data is stripped to {access_token} and the credential.update at line 97 stores key = {access_token, refresh_token}, dropping instance_url, id, signature, scope and token_type. On the second SalesforceCalendarService construction credentialKey.instance_url is undefined, so jsforce.Connection is built with no instance URL and falls back to the default login host, breaking every Salesforce operation — the integration is silently bricked for any host that enables credential sharing even though Salesforce is not part of the sync design at all.

[BUG] The webhook implements create-or-update as a findFirst followed by create/update with no transaction and no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId), so two concurrent deliveries for the same user+app both miss in findFirst and both execute create. Duplicate (userId, appId) credential rows are created — the codebase's own createOAuthAppCredential uses deleteMany-before-create precisely because no unique index exists — after which app-credential lookups return ambiguous rows, and the webhook's findFirst (no orderBy) updates an arbitrary one of the duplicates while a stale sibling keeps serving bookings; webhook delivery semantics make concurrent retries the normal case, not an edge case.

[BUG] The sync-mode fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortController, no response.ok check, and no fallback to the local refreshFunction on failure, and this refresh sits on the booking hot path for Zoom/Teams/O365/Lark/Webex/Google. When the parent application is slow or down, every token refresh on a sync-enabled host hangs the booking operation (Node's fetch has no default request timeout) or throws with no degradation, cascading a parent-app outage into all booking flows instead of falling back to the local refresh still sitting unused in refreshFunction — a shared single dependency whose exhaustion takes out every synced tenant.

[ADVISORY] The inline contract for the sync endpoint — "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date" — contradicts what this diff's consumers actually require: Lark's handleLarkError demands the Lark envelope {code, msg, data}, Google/Hubspot/Zoho need provider-native objects (and crash per the shape findings), and Zoom/O365/Webex/Teams each parse their app-native token bodies. A parent-app implementer who builds to the documented contract gets an endpoint that works for none of the apps: lark-calendar sync permanently fails in handleLarkError on the bare {access_token} body, with an error that gives no hint the response shape is the problem; the real per-app contract exists only in each consumer's error handler.

[ADVISORY] The appSlug values handed to the parent ('msteams' here, 'zoomvideo', 'google-calendar', 'hubspot', etc.) are bare magic strings with no compile-time tie to the appStoreMetadata keys and App-table slugs the webhook resolves them against, and 'msteams' matches no other identifier of this app anywhere in the diff (directory office365video, sibling references office365-calendar/office365_video). The parent keys its credentials by these strings and pushes them back to app-credential.ts, where prisma.app.findUnique({slug}) and appStoreMetadata[slug] must both resolve; if 'msteams' (or any of the nine hardcoded slugs) is not the exact seeded App slug / appStoreMetadata key, every MS Teams credential sync 404s in the webhook with no error surfaced anywhere on the Cal.com side, and Teams sync silently never works.

[ADVISORY] The webhook reads req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] without lowercasing the configured name, while Node lowercases every incoming header name, so any mixed-case value of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME (legal configuration, since HTTP header names are case-insensitive) misses the header entirely. An operator who sets the env var as "Calcom-Webhook-Secret" gets a 403 "Invalid webhook secret" on every delivery — a total, fail-closed outage of credential sync whose error message points at the secret rather than the header name; the .env.example comment ("Should be in lowercase") is unenforceable documentation standing in for a one-line toLowerCase() the code does not perform.

[ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces Office365's per-app error handling: the removed console.error was the only place the zod error and the raw MS response body were logged, the shared throw emits a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" with no app identifier or provider payload, and the failure mode escalates from log-and-continue (proceeding with the still-valid previous token) to a hard throw that aborts the refresh. Production Office365 auth incidents become undiagnosable — the MS response body appears nowhere in logs — and a transient provider anomaly that previously degraded to using the previous token now fails the entire calendar operation for the user; the same generic message is thrown by Zoom, Google and Salesforce, so the logs cannot even name the app.

[ADVISORY] The webhook persists JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)) into credential.key with no validation against the target app's credential schema, even though every OAuth callback path in this codebase zod-validates token payloads before storing them. A parent pushing a malformed or truncated payload (wrong app's keys, missing expiry_date or refresh_token) creates a credential row that passes storage and then throws inside the app's CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter at first use, failing that user's bookings with parse errors that give no hint the bad data arrived via the sync webhook — the operator's only recovery path is re-running the parent push blind.

[BUG] GoogleCalendarService persists parseRefreshTokenResponse's return value — the entire zod SafeParseResult ({success, data}) — directly as Credential.key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) value. Every Google Calendar token refresh on the default configuration (credential sync disabled) writes {success:true, data:{...}} into the credential row; on the next load getGoogleAuth reads credential.key, finds no top-level access_token/refresh_token, and throws, permanently breaking the user's Google Calendar integration and every booking that uses it until the app is reinstalled — the stored wrapper shape is unreadable by the app.

[BUG] The sync branch returns the raw fetch Response while all seven call sites were written against the provider-specific shapes the default branch returns (gaxios res.data for Google, a HubspotToken object for HubSpot, an axios response with .data for Zoho CRM/Bigin, provider-envelope JSON for the Lark/Zoom/MS handlers). Setting CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT crashes Google refresh with TypeError (token = res?.data is undefined on a fetch Response, then token.access_token), crashes Zoho CRM/Bigin evaluating tokenInfo.data.error on undefined, makes HubSpot store undefined token fields, and feeds Lark/Zoom handlers bodies in the wrong shape — the credential-sync feature fails at runtime for most apps the moment it is enabled.

[BUG] The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (duplicate key, second wins), so minimumTokenResponseSchema is really {access_token: string} and zod's default unknown-key stripping deletes every other field of the response — it does not 'assume any property with a number is the expiry' as the comments claim. Once the sync env vars are set, every parseRefreshTokenResponse caller silently switches to this schema: Salesforce (which refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com regardless of sync) persists a key of only {access_token, refresh_token}, stripping instance_url from a response that contained it, so the next jsforce.Connection is built with instanceUrl undefined and all Salesforce calls fail; Office365 never receives a new expiry, so it re-refreshes (sync-endpoint POST plus a credential DB write) on every operation.

[BUG] Bigin passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' userId argument — every sibling call site passes credential.userId — so the sync request posts the credential's own DB id as calcomUserId.
