With credential sync enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), this would send a credential row id as `calcomUserId`, causing failed user lookup or wrong token association at the parent endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The outbound fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication (no shared secret, no auth header), while the inbound webhook direction enforces CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The operator's token-issuing endpoint has no shipped way to authenticate Cal.com's calls — anyone who learns the endpoint URL can request live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary cal.com user ids, defeating the secret-based trust model the feature itself establishes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, Cal.com performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication material (no shared secret, no auth header, no signature). By contrast, the inbound webhook endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) explicitly authenticates requests via `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`. The diff introduces an asymmetric trust model where Cal.com has no built-in way to prove its identity to the external credential-sync endpoint, which is a security defect in the introduced feature surface (callers who can hit that endpoint can request token refreshes keyed only by `calcomUserId`/`appSlug`, unless the operator implements separate protections not provided here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler performs no req.method check and calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no try/catch, so schema, decryption and JSON errors propagate unhandled. A GET request, or a correctly-secreted but malformed payload (missing body, non-JSON ciphertext, non-32-byte encryption key), returns a bare 500 instead of the 400/405 a webhook contract needs, leaving the integrating operator with no diagnosable error from their own misconfiguration.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler never checks `req.method`, so non-POST requests (e.g., GET) will still proceed to `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, which throws on invalid/empty bodies. Additionally, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(...)`, `symmetricDecrypt(...)`, and `JSON.parse(...)` are all called without any try/catch or error-to-HTTP mapping, so malformed payloads or misconfiguration (e.g., bad ciphertext, empty/invalid `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) will bubble exceptions and typically produce a generic 500 response rather than a diagnosable 4xx (400/405) response. This behavior is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Coverage gap: the diff ships a new externally-callable webhook (secret auth, AES decryption, credential upsert), two new utilities, and rewired token-refresh/persistence across ten integrations with zero test files — a scan of the diff finds none under any test path or test-name pattern. Regressions like the parse→safeParse wrapper change that corrupts Google credential keys pass straight to production because no assertion anywhere in the diff covers a token-refresh round trip or the webhook's auth/decrypt/upsert behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s example regression is verifiable in the diff: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result object (with `.success`/`.data`), but `GoogleCalendarService` now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists that directly to Prisma (`data: { key }`). This would store the parse-result wrapper instead of the credential payload, corrupting Google credential keys on refresh. While the finding also notes there are no tests added (true from the diff), the cited corruption is an actual correctness defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor path now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a credential DB write on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, replacing jsforce's previous lazy on-demand refresh. Every Salesforce-connected booking or availability check incurs a round trip to login.salesforce.com and a credential row update even when the stored token is minutes old, multiplying Salesforce API usage, latency, and DB write load on the hot booking path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a token refresh HTTP call to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then immediately persists the refreshed token via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection`. This refresh+DB write occurs in the service initialization path (not gated by token age/expiry), so constructing `SalesforceCalendarService` will always incur the network round-trip and a credential row update even if the existing token is still valid. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern (increased latency, Salesforce token endpoint usage, DB write amplification) rather than a definite functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync gate requires a non-null userId, silently excluding team-owned credentials (userId null) from credential sync with no error, log, or documentation of the exclusion, while the webhook schema equally only accepts a user id. Self-hosters running the sync model do not configure their own OAuth client secrets (the parent app owns them), so team-connected apps fall back to native refresh with missing client credentials and team bookings fail opaquely while per-user bookings keep working.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably restricts the new credential-sync path to user-owned credentials only: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., userId)` only uses `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `userId` is truthy (`if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId)`) and otherwise silently falls back to the native refresh function, with no log/diagnostic. Additionally, the new webhook API `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` only accepts `userId` in its Zod schema (no team identifier), so team-owned credentials (`credential.userId === null`) cannot be synced via this mechanism. The claim that this will necessarily cause team bookings to fail due to missing OAuth client credentials depends on external self-hoster configuration not shown in the diff, so it’s an incomplete/edge-case design concern rather than a definitively provable defect from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint JSON.parses and persists whatever the parent sends without validating the decrypted payload against the target app's credential schema, even though every refresh path in this same diff enforces zod schemas on the same key field. A parent app pushing a structurally wrong payload (missing access_token, wrong field names, or even a non-object JSON value) receives a 200, and the end user's bookings crash later inside the calendar service with errors that give no hint the webhook seeded the bad credential.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) decrypts `reqBody.keys`, `JSON.parse`s it, and then directly persists it to `prisma.credential` as `key` without validating the decrypted payload against any app-specific credential schema (it only validates `keys` as a string via zod on the request body). This allows structurally invalid/non-object decrypted JSON to be stored (e.g., missing required fields like `access_token`), which can later break consumers that assume valid credential shapes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) and this code persists that envelope directly as the credential key, replacing the flat credential object that googleCredentialSchema.parse() previously returned. The first Google Calendar token refresh after this deploys writes {success:true, data:{...}} into Credential.key, so every subsequent GoogleCalendarService construction reads credential.key.access_token and credential.key.refresh_token as undefined and all Google Calendar operations fail for every user on every deployment, credential sharing enabled or not.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope), not the parsed token object (`.data`). However, in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store the envelope into `Credential.key` instead of the flat credential payload (previously produced by `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`), breaking later reads that expect `credential.key.access_token` / `refresh_token` to exist at the top level. This defect is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sharing is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint's raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data expecting the gaxios response shape and then dereferences token.access_token unguarded. With the feature enabled, res.data is undefined on a fetch Response and token.access_token throws a TypeError inside every Google Calendar token refresh, so Google Calendar fails exactly in the configuration this PR exists to enable.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it performs `fetch(...)` and returns the raw Fetch `Response`. But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller does `const token = res?.data;` and then unguardedly dereferences `token.access_token`. A Fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property (unlike the gaxios shape returned by `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...).res`), so with credential sharing enabled `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw, breaking Google Calendar refresh in the enabled configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint's raw fetch Response to seven call sites that each expect an app-native shape (gaxios .data, axios .data, HubSpot SDK token object) with no adaptation layer anywhere. The moment sync is enabled zoho-bigin (tokenInfo.data.error) and zohocrm (zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) throw TypeError reading 'error' of undefined because a fetch Response has no .data, hubspot receives a Response typed as HubspotToken so its expires_in arithmetic yields a NaN expiry, and lark/webex/zoom/office365/msteams receive response bodies their handlers never parse — the feature breaks every integration it was written to cover.

adjudication.rationale:
Verified in diff: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns either the integration’s native refresh result (axios response / HubSpot SDK object / fetch Response / gaxios `res`) OR, when sync is enabled, it **always** returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` from `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (no parsing/adaptation). Multiple call sites still assume native shapes:
- Zoho Bigin: `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...axios.post...)` then `tokenInfo.data.error` (but a fetch `Response` has no `.data`) → runtime TypeError.
- Zoho CRM: same pattern `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` → TypeError.
- HubSpot: `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...hubspotClient...)`; sync path returns `Response`, so fields like `expires_in` become `undefined`, producing wrong expiry calculations (NaN) or later failures.
- Google Calendar: expects gaxios-like `{res}` and does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` but sync path returns `Response` so `res?.data` is undefined → crashes.
This mismatch is introduced by the new sync feature path and will break integrations when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This call passes credentialId (the credential row primary key) as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, which is serialized to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. When sync is enabled the parent application receives a credential id where the contract (and every sibling call site, which passes credential.userId) says Cal.com user id, so zoho-bigin token sync matches no user — or the wrong user where the ids numerically collide — and zoho-bigin credentials silently never refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the third parameter is explicitly `userId: number | null` and, when syncing is enabled, it is serialized as `calcomUserId` in the POST body. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call site passes `credentialId` as that third argument (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`), while other updated call sites consistently pass `credential.userId`. This mismaps the contract and would send a credential row id to the sync endpoint instead of the Cal.com user id, causing refresh/token sync to fail or target the wrong user if ids collide.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites the parsed data's refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token' whenever the response lacks one, and callers persist that data as the stored credential key. The sync response by design contains only access_token and expiry, so with sharing enabled the zoom/salesforce/office365 credential updates write the literal 'refresh_token' over the user's real refresh token, destroying the only material that can re-authorize; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset or the flag reverted, those integrations are permanently broken until each user manually reconnects the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it validates refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not require `refresh_token`), and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if missing. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is merged into `o365AuthCredentials` via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, so the literal string overwrites the real stored `refresh_token` and is then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: o365AuthCredentials } })`. That is data loss and can break future re-auth when sync is disabled. (Note: the diff’s new Salesforce refresh path explicitly preserves the old refresh token, so that part of the finding isn’t fully accurate, but the core defect is clearly present.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The spread ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) merges parseRefreshTokenResponse's sync-mode output — only {access_token} plus the injected literal refresh_token:'refresh_token' — into the office365 credential that is then written to the database. Enabling credential sharing on a deployment with Office365 calendars replaces each user's stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token' on the first refresh, so the credential can never be refreshed locally again and the user must reconnect the app.

[BUG] The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to identical literal stringified-schema property names, so minimumTokenResponseSchema implements none of its commented intent ('any property with a number is the expiry') and enforces nothing beyond access_token — no expiry property is ever validated. In sync mode a token response missing the expiry field parses successfully, so expiry_date/expires_in are never updated and office365/google credentials fail expiry checks or re-refresh on every operation, while the strict per-app schemas (googleCredentialSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) are silently discarded whenever the flag is on.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to literal string keys (e.g., Zod’s stringified schema names), not an index signature/catchall, so the schema does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior. Instead it either (a) incorrectly requires a property with that literal key to exist (likely causing sync-mode parsing to fail and throw), and/or (b) never truly validates presence of an expiry field. Additionally, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, the code intentionally switches from the per-app schema to this broken minimum schema, so strict validation is effectively bypassed/invalidated in that mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This PR adds an ungated Salesforce token refresh — a POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update — that executes on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens, and is not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED unlike every other behavior change in the diff. Every Salesforce calendar operation on every deployment (including ones that will never use credential sharing) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip and a DB write per service construction, and the response.statusText !== 'OK' gate converts any proxy that strips the reason phrase or any Salesforce error body into a thrown HttpError that kills the operation — a scope expansion traceable to no stated requirement.

[BUG] Salesforce's new refresh path never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so even with credential sharing enabled a Salesforce credential delivered by the app-credential webhook (refresh token issued to the parent app's OAuth client) is refreshed locally with this instance's consumer_key/consumer_secret. Salesforce rejects the mismatched client with invalid_grant, the statusText check throws HttpError 400, and the Salesforce integration is broken in exactly the configuration this PR exists to enable — the invariant 'shared credentials refresh via the sync endpoint' holds for nine apps and is violated for the tenth.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, most integrations’ token refresh logic is routed through the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper (e.g. Google, Hubspot, Lark, Office365, Zoom, Webex, Zoho) so that when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, refresh happens via the external sync endpoint. The new Salesforce refresh logic in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` instead performs a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` using `client_id: consumer_key` and `client_secret: consumer_secret` and does not call `refreshOAuthTokens` at all. Given this PR’s stated goal (shared credentials / sync endpoint), Salesforce is the outlier and will not use the sync endpoint even when enabled, making the feature inconsistent and likely broken for Salesforce in that configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The outbound sync request POSTs only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication of any kind — no shared secret, signature, or auth header, and no way for the operator to add one — even though the inbound webhook direction shipped in the same PR requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can enumerate sequential calcomUserIds against the public app-slug list and harvest live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users of the Cal.com deployment, because the parent app has no Cal.com-presented credential to verify and the hard-coded body leaves no place to put one.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, the code does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth headers, signature, or shared secret included, and no configuration hook to add one. This contrasts with the inbound webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) which enforces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The diff therefore introduces an unauthenticated token-sync request pattern that could let an exposed `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` be queried with arbitrary `calcomUserId`/`appSlug` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with no HTTP method guard and no error handling, and the later JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is equally unprotected. A GET request, a POST with a malformed body, or a keys value encrypted under a different key throws an unhandled ZodError or decryption error and returns a 500 instead of the 403/404 the endpoint's own convention promises, so the parent application cannot distinguish a contract violation from a Cal.com outage.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, `handler` has no `req.method` guard (e.g., to restrict to POST), and it calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` directly. `zod.parse` throws on invalid/missing body (likely for GET or malformed POST), and the subsequent `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` can also throw on bad ciphertext/wrong key. There is no try/catch or safeParse-based handling, so these cases will bubble up as unhandled exceptions and return a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response like the rest of the handler’s 403/404 conventions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect URI is rewritten from the config-driven `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` to the hardcoded literal 'zoho-bigin', a change unrelated to credential sync that nothing in the PR's stated intent explains. The install URL is silently decoupled from config.json, so any future slug or routing change leaves zoho-bigin OAuth installs failing with a redirect_uri mismatch, and a reviewer cannot trace this line to any requirement in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts`, the redirect URI is changed from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to the hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback``. This is verifiable in the diff and does decouple the OAuth redirect URI from `config.json` (even though `appConfig` is still imported). Whether this is a *current* bug depends on whether `appConfig.slug` is already `zoho-bigin` (not shown in the diff), so the claim of immediate redirect_uri mismatch can’t be proven here; however, the maintainability/traceability concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so its runtime value is the raw AES-256 encryption key string (or empty string), not a boolean. Any log line, error report, or serialized config that includes this exported flag prints the key that decrypts every synced app credential, and consumers that compare === true or persist the value get the secret itself instead of an on/off flag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`. In JS/TS, `a && b` returns `b` when `a` is truthy, so when both env vars are set this exported value becomes the raw `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` string (and can also become the raw webhook secret when the second operand is falsy), not a boolean. This is a security/correctness defect for an exported flag: any code that serializes/prints/compares the flag as a boolean could inadvertently propagate the secret value, and the name strongly implies it should be `true|false`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Replacing refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse plus the explicit console.error of the zodError and the Microsoft response with parseRefreshTokenResponse deletes the only diagnostics on this refresh path and substitutes a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' throw. Operators debugging the notoriously flaky Office365 token refresh now get no provider response payload and no zod detail in the logs, turning a previously diagnosable failure into an opaque error with no actionable fields.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff replaces `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` plus an explicit `console.error(...)` block (logging zodError and the MS response payload) with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, and removes the only logging on failure. The new helper throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` without logging provider payload or zod details, making Office365 refresh failures less diagnosable. This is a diff-grounded observability/operability regression rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's two computed keys both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (z.string().toString() on a Zod schema instance returns Object.prototype.toString's output, and the second computed key overwrites the first), so the sync-mode schema is really z.object({access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional()}) which validates only access_token and strips every other property — the opposite of the commented intent "Allow other properties in the token response". On any host with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every sync-mode parse returns only {access_token}: GoogleCalendarService.ts:96 persists that as the entire credential.key (destroying refresh_token and expiry_date), Office365CalendarService.ts:263 merges it so expiry_date is never updated (stale expiry forces a parent round-trip on every operation), and the app-specific schemas (zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) become dead code, so any parent response with a string access_token is accepted no matter what else it contains or lacks.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines two computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate immediately to string keys (very likely the same literal, e.g. "[object Object]"), so the second overwrites the first and the schema does not actually accept arbitrary keys/expiry fields as intended. Additionally, `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, so in “sync mode” (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the safeParse result will retain essentially only `access_token` (plus the function then mutates in a placeholder `refresh_token`), dropping fields like `expiry_date`/real `refresh_token`. This aligns with the diff’s usage: e.g. Google (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) passes credentials through `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` before persisting, and Office365 merges from the parsed result, so stripped fields would cause stale/missing token data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token whenever the sync-mode schema is selected (a schema that by construction can never produce a real refresh token), and every caller persists that sentinel into credential.key. Zoom (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts merges {...credential.key, ...parsedToken.data}) and Office365 (CalendarService.ts:263 merge) overwrite the user's real provider refresh_token with the string "refresh_token", and Google stores it wholesale; the moment CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is removed, or for team-owned credentials where userId is null (refreshOAuthTokens takes the local-refresh path at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 while parsing still uses the sync schema because its condition omits userId), the stored fake token is used against the provider and the credential is permanently bricked — every affected user must re-authenticate every app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which (by design) does not include `refresh_token`. The function then unconditionally injects `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. Call sites then persist/merge this into stored credentials, e.g. Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` and then updates Prisma, which will overwrite the real `refresh_token` with the sentinel string. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`’s condition does not consider `userId`, so even when `refreshOAuthTokens` falls back to the local refresh path for `userId` null (team-owned credentials), parsing can still use the minimum schema and inject the sentinel, causing the stored refresh token to be corrupted as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15), but this code reads res?.data — the googleapis Gaxios response shape — which is undefined on a fetch Response, so token.access_token throws a TypeError. google-calendar token refresh never succeeds on sync-enabled hosts: the TypeError hits the surrounding try/catch, the credential is never updated, and the service proceeds with an expired access token, so every calendar operation for that user fails with Google 401s — the flagship app of this PR cannot work with the feature the PR implements.
matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: in sync/credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response lacking a .data field, so reading res?.data yields undefined and accessing token.access_token throws at runtime due to inconsistent return shape assumptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code assigns it to hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken and the following code reads .expires_in/.access_token directly off it — properties a fetch Response does not have. hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in is undefined so the expiry is computed as NaN and hubspotCredentialSchema.parse throws on the Response object (which lacks every HubspotToken field), so HubSpot token refresh always fails whenever sync is enabled and HubSpot operations requiring a fresh token break.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result of `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is assigned to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken`, i.e. the calling code is written as if it receives a HubSpot token payload object rather than a `Response`. This is a real behavioral mismatch introduced by the diff: in sync mode the returned value will not have HubSpot token fields (it will be a `Response`), so downstream access to token properties would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the very next statement reads tokenInfo.data — the axios response shape — which is undefined on a fetch Response, so !tokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes on every attempt when sync is enabled; the Bigin credential is never refreshed and the CRM integration fails for sync-enabled hosts.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh call was changed to `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but the subsequent logic still assumes an Axios response shape (`if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`). The new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (added in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a `fetch()` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, and a `Response` does not have `.data`. That makes `tokenInfo.data` undefined and `tokenInfo.data.error` will throw at runtime in sync mode, breaking Zoho Bigin refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the next statement reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data — the axios response shape — which is undefined on a fetch Response, so !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho CRM token refresh crashes on every attempt when sync is enabled; the credential is never refreshed and the Zoho CRM integration fails for sync-enabled hosts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens`, which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set and a `userId` is provided, returns a `fetch(...)` Response object (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns `const zohoCrmTokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. A `fetch` Response does not have a `.data` property (that’s an axios shape), so in sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a TypeError. This matches the reported crash path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BiginCalendarService passes credentialId (the Credential row's primary key, credential.id) as refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter named userId, where every other call site in this diff passes credential.userId. In sync mode the parent app receives calcomUserId=<credential id> — a value from the unrelated Credential id sequence — and either finds no user or returns the tokens of whichever user happens to own that id, so Bigin stores and operates on another user's Zoho credentials (cross-user CRM data corruption); the wrong binding is invisible because non-sync mode ignores the argument entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes a value named `credentialId` into `refreshOAuthTokens`’ third parameter, which is explicitly treated as a Cal.com *user* id (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()` in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Every other updated call site passes `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the credential row’s PK (as the name strongly implies), sync mode will send the wrong identifier to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, potentially returning/overwriting tokens for the wrong user; non-sync mode would mask this because the argument is ignored there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction — no expiry/isExpired guard, and no routing through refreshOAuthTokens — creating a parallel refresh path that duplicates jsforce's own OAuth refresh and bypasses the sync abstraction every other app in this PR uses. Every availability check and booking involving a Salesforce-connected user now makes a login.salesforce.com round trip (which counts against the org's Salesforce API/login limits) plus a DB write, even on hosts that never enable credential sharing: hot-path latency and org API-quota exhaustion are added to all Salesforce booking flows, and concurrent constructions race read-modify-write on credential.key.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now unconditionally performs a token refresh request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`) and then immediately writes the refreshed token into the DB (`await prisma.credential.update(...)`) before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no expiry/"isExpired"-style guard shown, so this refresh+DB-write happens whenever this code path runs, and it also does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` abstraction used elsewhere in the PR. The added network call and write on what is likely a hot path is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse selects the sync-mode minimumTokenResponseSchema based on global env vars even though Salesforce obtains its response directly from login.salesforce.com (it never routes through the sync endpoint), so on sync-enabled hosts accessTokenParsed.data is stripped to {access_token} and the credential.update at line 97 stores key = {access_token, refresh_token}, dropping instance_url, id, signature, scope and token_type. On the second SalesforceCalendarService construction credentialKey.instance_url is undefined, so jsforce.Connection is built with no instance URL and falls back to the default login host, breaking every Salesforce operation — the integration is silently bricked for any host that enables credential sharing even though Salesforce is not part of the sync design at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function ignores the caller-provided schema whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is truthy, and instead validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, Salesforce refreshes tokens directly from `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` (not via `refreshOAuthTokens` / the sync endpoint), but still calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`. Therefore on hosts with credential sharing + sync endpoint enabled, Salesforce token responses will be parsed against the wrong schema, which can drop required Salesforce fields or fail validation, and then `prisma.credential.update` persists an incomplete/invalid key. This is a correctness defect introduced by the diff and can brick the Salesforce integration under those env settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook implements create-or-update as a findFirst followed by create/update with no transaction and no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId), so two concurrent deliveries for the same user+app both miss in findFirst and both execute create. Duplicate (userId, appId) credential rows are created — the codebase's own createOAuthAppCredential uses deleteMany-before-create precisely because no unique index exists — after which app-credential lookups return ambiguous rows, and the webhook's findFirst (no orderBy) updates an arbitrary one of the duplicates while a stale sibling keeps serving bookings; webhook delivery semantics make concurrent retries the normal case, not an edge case.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the create-or-update logic is implemented as `findFirst` followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`, with no transaction/locking and no `upsert`. This is a real, diff-grounded race condition pattern: concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no row” and both attempt `create`. However, the finding’s stronger claim (that duplicates will definitely be created because there is no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`) cannot be verified from this diff since the Prisma schema/DB constraints are not shown here. So the concurrency concern is valid, but whether it manifests as duplicate rows vs. a unique-constraint error is not provable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync-mode fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortController, no response.ok check, and no fallback to the local refreshFunction on failure, and this refresh sits on the booking hot path for Zoom/Teams/O365/Lark/Webex/Google. When the parent application is slow or down, every token refresh on a sync-enabled host hangs the booking operation (Node's fetch has no default request timeout) or throws with no degradation, cascading a parent-app outage into all booking flows instead of falling back to the local refresh still sitting unused in refreshFunction — a shared single dependency whose exhaustion takes out every synced tenant.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and returns the raw `Response` without any timeout/AbortController, without checking `response.ok`, and without any try/catch fallback to `refreshFunction()` on failure. This is directly used by multiple integrations’ token refresh flows in this diff (e.g., Zoom/Office365/Webex/Lark/Google/Hubspot). As written, a slow/down sync endpoint can stall indefinitely (no timeout) or propagate errors with no degradation, turning a parent-app outage into booking/integration failures for sync-enabled hosts. Additionally, some call sites expect a non-`fetch` response shape (e.g., Google expects `res?.data`), so returning a `fetch` `Response` from the sync-path can also break at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The inline contract for the sync endpoint — "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date" — contradicts what this diff's consumers actually require: Lark's handleLarkError demands the Lark envelope {code, msg, data}, Google/Hubspot/Zoho need provider-native objects (and crash per the shape findings), and Zoom/O365/Webex/Teams each parse their app-native token bodies. A parent-app implementer who builds to the documented contract gets an endpoint that works for none of the apps: lark-calendar sync permanently fails in handleLarkError on the bare {access_token} body, with an error that gives no hint the response shape is the problem; the real per-app contract exists only in each consumer's error handler.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens()` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, calls `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns that response (a Fetch `Response`) while its call sites continue to expect provider-native/token-library-native shapes. Examples in the diff: Google Calendar expects `res?.data` after `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (but Fetch `Response` has no `.data`), and Lark passes the returned value to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which (by its type usage) expects a Lark API response that can be parsed as `RefreshTokenResp`, not a generic `{access_token, expiry}` contract. Similarly, Hubspot/Zoho callers type the return as token objects/axios responses, but in sync mode they would receive a Fetch `Response`. This makes the inline contract comment in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` (“response should only contain the access token and expiry date”) incompatible with how the diff’s consumers actually handle the returned value, causing broken runtime behavior when the sync feature is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The appSlug values handed to the parent ('msteams' here, 'zoomvideo', 'google-calendar', 'hubspot', etc.) are bare magic strings with no compile-time tie to the appStoreMetadata keys and App-table slugs the webhook resolves them against, and 'msteams' matches no other identifier of this app anywhere in the diff (directory office365video, sibling references office365-calendar/office365_video). The parent keys its credentials by these strings and pushes them back to app-credential.ts, where prisma.app.findUnique({slug}) and appStoreMetadata[slug] must both resolve; if 'msteams' (or any of the nine hardcoded slugs) is not the exact seeded App slug / appStoreMetadata key, every MS Teams credential sync 404s in the webhook with no error surfaced anywhere on the Cal.com side, and Teams sync silently never works.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce multiple hard-coded `appSlug` magic strings passed into `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (e.g. `"msteams"` in `packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `"zoomvideo"`, `"google-calendar"`, `"hubspot"`, etc.). Nothing in the diff provides a compile-time/typed linkage between these literals and the canonical slugs used elsewhere (e.g. the `appStoreMetadata[...]` lookup and `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). However, the finding’s specific claim that this will definitively cause webhook 404s (because these literals are pushed “back to app-credential.ts”) is not directly verifiable from the diff: the webhook’s `reqBody.appSlug` is supplied by an external caller, and the diff doesn’t show that it is sourced from these literals. So the concrete drift risk is real and diff-grounded, but the “will 404 and silently never works” part can’t be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook reads req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] without lowercasing the configured name, while Node lowercases every incoming header name, so any mixed-case value of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME (legal configuration, since HTTP header names are case-insensitive) misses the header entirely. An operator who sets the env var as "Calcom-Webhook-Secret" gets a 403 "Invalid webhook secret" on every delivery — a total, fail-closed outage of credential sync whose error message points at the secret rather than the header name; the .env.example comment ("Should be in lowercase") is unenforceable documentation standing in for a one-line toLowerCase() the code does not perform.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the secret check indexes `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without normalizing the configured header name. In Node/Next, `req.headers` keys are lowercased, so if an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to a mixed-case value like `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`, the lookup will miss and the comparison will fail, returning 403 "Invalid webhook secret" for all requests. The `.env.example` comment requests lowercase but the code does not enforce it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces Office365's per-app error handling: the removed console.error was the only place the zod error and the raw MS response body were logged, the shared throw emits a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" with no app identifier or provider payload, and the failure mode escalates from log-and-continue (proceeding with the still-valid previous token) to a hard throw that aborts the refresh. Production Office365 auth incidents become undiagnosable — the MS response body appears nowhere in logs — and a transient provider anomaly that previously degraded to using the previous token now fails the entire calendar operation for the user; the same generic message is thrown by Zoom, Google and Salesforce, so the logs cannot even name the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, logged `console.error(...)` including the zod error and `responseJson`, then continued (no throw) and still updated the credential with the existing `o365AuthCredentials`. The diff replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails and contains no provider/app context or payload logging. This is a diff-verifiable change in failure behavior (from log-and-continue to hard throw) and removes the only logged MS response body, reducing diagnosability; the same generic throw is reused across multiple providers in this PR (e.g., Zoom/Google/Salesforce).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook persists JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)) into credential.key with no validation against the target app's credential schema, even though every OAuth callback path in this codebase zod-validates token payloads before storing them. A parent pushing a malformed or truncated payload (wrong app's keys, missing expiry_date or refresh_token) creates a credential row that passes storage and then throws inside the app's CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter at first use, failing that user's bookings with parse errors that give no hint the bad data arrived via the sync webhook — the operator's only recovery path is re-running the parent push blind.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the decrypted payload is accepted as arbitrary JSON (`const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`) and written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` with no validation against any app-specific credential schema (only `appStoreMetadata` is checked for slug/type). This makes it possible for a well-authenticated caller (secret header + encryption key) to persist malformed/truncated/wrong-shape credential data that will only be rejected later when CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter code attempts zod parsing on first use, causing runtime failures. The diff shows many OAuth flows continue to zod-validate refreshed token structures before updating credentials, highlighting the inconsistency the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GoogleCalendarService persists parseRefreshTokenResponse's return value — the entire zod SafeParseResult ({success, data}) — directly as Credential.key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) value. Every Google Calendar token refresh on the default configuration (credential sync disabled) writes {success:true, data:{...}} into the credential row; on the next load getGoogleAuth reads credential.key, finds no top-level access_token/refresh_token, and throws, permanently breaking the user's Google Calendar integration and every booking that uses it until the app is reinstalled — the stored wrapper shape is unreadable by the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh logic was changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed credential object) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and the result is persisted directly as `Credential.key` (`data: { key }`). But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not `refreshTokenResponse.data`. Persisting that wrapper shape would replace the credential key object with an unreadable structure for code expecting top-level `access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc., matching the finding’s described breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync branch returns the raw fetch Response while all seven call sites were written against the provider-specific shapes the default branch returns (gaxios res.data for Google, a HubspotToken object for HubSpot, an axios response with .data for Zoho CRM/Bigin, provider-envelope JSON for the Lark/Zoom/MS handlers). Setting CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT crashes Google refresh with TypeError (token = res?.data is undefined on a fetch Response, then token.access_token), crashes Zoho CRM/Bigin evaluating tokenInfo.data.error on undefined, makes HubSpot store undefined token fields, and feeds Lark/Zoom handlers bodies in the wrong shape — the credential-sync feature fails at runtime for most apps the moment it is enabled.

[BUG] The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (duplicate key, second wins), so minimumTokenResponseSchema is really {access_token: string} and zod's default unknown-key stripping deletes every other field of the response — it does not 'assume any property with a number is the expiry' as the comments claim. Once the sync env vars are set, every parseRefreshTokenResponse caller silently switches to this schema: Salesforce (which refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com regardless of sync) persists a key of only {access_token, refresh_token}, stripping instance_url from a response that contained it, so the next jsforce.Connection is built with instanceUrl undefined and all Salesforce calls fail; Office365 never receives a new expiry, so it re-refreshes (sync-endpoint POST plus a credential DB write) on every operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate to a single literal string key at runtime (commonly `"[object Object]"`), so this does not match “any numeric property” as the comment claims. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, when the min schema path is activated (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` && `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), most token response fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc.) will be dropped. This can directly break integrations relying on those fields (e.g., Office365 expiry handling; Salesforce persisting refreshed tokens without `instance_url`), matching the finding’s core claim about schema behavior and resulting data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Bigin passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' userId argument — every sibling call site passes credential.userId — so the sync request posts the credential's own DB id as calcomUserId. In sync mode the parent app receives a credential id where the protocol's calcomUserId is expected, resolves no user (or the wrong one), and its returned tokens are persisted under this credential — Bigin credential sync never works and can silently attach the wrong entity's tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call is `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` treats its 3rd argument as `userId` and, in sync mode, posts it as `calcomUserId` (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). Every other updated call site in the diff passes `credential.userId`, so passing `credentialId` here will send the credential record id instead of the Cal.com user id, breaking credential sync for Bigin (or mapping tokens to the wrong user) when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is the expression `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which evaluates to the raw encryption-key string, not a boolean. The exported 'feature flag' carries the master credential-encryption key value into every module that imports it; any log line, error report, or debug serialization of the flag (the most natural thing to print for a flag) leaks the key that decrypts every synced credential — wrap it in Boolean() to fix.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`, which in JS/TS evaluates to the *second operand* (the raw `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` string) when both are truthy, not a boolean. This value is then imported across multiple modules in the diff (e.g., webhook handler and OAuth refresh utilities), so treating it as a feature flag risks accidental logging/serialization of the constant and leaking the master encryption key. Wrapping with `Boolean(...)` (or `!!(...)`) would avoid exporting the secret value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SalesforceCalendarService construction now unconditionally performs a live token refresh against login.salesforce.com plus a credential DB write on every instantiation, where previously it built jsforce.Connection from the stored key and let jsforce refresh lazily. Every Salesforce calendar operation gains a Salesforce OAuth round-trip and a DB write (inviting rate limiting or refresh-token lockout), and a transient refresh failure now throws HttpError 400 before any operation even when the stored access token was still valid — previously-working Salesforce installs start failing on network blips, a default-path behavior change unrelated to the credential-sync opt-in.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new code unconditionally performs a refresh-token HTTP POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `jsforce.Connection` (see added block starting with `const response = await fetch(...)` and subsequent DB update). This makes every instantiation depend on a live Salesforce round-trip and triggers a DB write even if the stored access token is still valid. It also now throws early (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })`) on transient failures, which can break previously-working operations. This behavior is not gated by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` / sync endpoint, so it affects the default path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] HTTP success is detected via `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of response.ok. Any 200 response whose reason phrase is not exactly 'OK' (intermediaries or runtimes that normalize or omit reason phrases, HTTP/2 responses) is treated as failure and throws HttpError 400 despite a valid token body, killing the Salesforce integration behind such proxies.
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the integration determines success of the OAuth refresh response by checking `response.statusText` (expecting "OK") instead of using `response.ok`, which is unreliable and can misclassify successful responses, leading to use of stale/invalid credentials and auth failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor replaced refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse plus a console.error of the zod error and the raw Microsoft response with a helper that throws the generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', deleting the only diagnostics on this path. When Microsoft changes its token response fields (the historically flaky case this logging existed for), operators get a message with no field-level error and no record of responseJson, turning a five-minute diagnosis into a blind outage investigation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, `console.error(...)` including both the Zod error and the raw `responseJson`. The refactor replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails and does not log either the schema error details or `responseJson`. This concretely removes the only diagnostics on this failure path, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no try/catch and never checks req.method, so input errors throw instead of returning the 4xx the surrounding code deliberately uses for every other input problem. A GET probe, a request with a missing or ill-typed body, or a wrongly-encrypted keys payload produces an unhandled ZodError or decrypt exception and a Next 500 — breaking the endpoint's own 403/404 contract, leaving the parent-app integrator unable to distinguish auth rejection from server bugs, and dumping stack traces into server logs on every malformed attempt.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does not check `req.method` (so a GET/other method will still execute) and it calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch. Both `zod.parse` and decrypt/JSON.parse can throw on malformed/missing body or invalid ciphertext, which would surface as an unhandled exception (Next.js 500) rather than the explicit 4xx responses used elsewhere in this handler (403/404).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shared webhook secret is compared with plain !== string inequality rather than a timing-safe comparison. An attacker who can repeatedly hit /api/webhook/app-credential and measure response times can byte-by-byte recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, then forge credential writes for arbitrary userIds — crypto.timingSafeEqual is the standard fix.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret check uses a direct inequality comparison: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is not a timing-safe comparison and can, in principle, leak information about `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` through timing differences. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Google refresh path persists the entire zod safeParse wrapper — `{success, data}` — as `credential.key`, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the raw safeParse result while the code it replaces stored the flat output of `googleCredentialSchema.parse()`. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *entire* Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not the parsed `data` payload. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal junk string "refresh_token" into `data.refresh_token` whenever the parsed response lacks a refresh_token, and callers persist that parsed data directly into `credential.key`. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the parsed refresh response lacks a `refresh_token` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` evaluate to the same string "[object Object]" (Zod schemas do not override toString) and collide — the second silently overwrites the first — so the schema enforces nothing beyond `access_token` and z.object strips every other field from the parsed output. In sharing mode the parsed data contains only `access_token`: the `expiry_date`/`expires_in` values the sync endpoint returns are dropped (Office365CalendarService persists a stale expiry and re-refreshes on every call or trusts an expired token; Zoom/office365video lose the expiry entirely), and the documented "any numeric property is the expiry" validation never runs, so a misconfigured parent endpoint silently poisons stored credentials instead of being rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to express “any numeric property is the expiry” via computed keys: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In a JS object literal these become fixed string property names (whatever `toString()` returns), not a wildcard/index signature, so they will not match real token fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in`. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, in sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the safeParse result’s `.data` will retain essentially only `access_token` (and possibly those fixed-name keys if present), dropping expiry fields. The diff shows this return value is then used to update credentials (e.g., Office365 uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and spreads `tokenResponse.data`), so expiry can be lost/stale as the finding describes. The specific claim that both computed keys evaluate to the same string and collide is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone, but the underlying schema logic is clearly incorrect and causes the described data loss/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sharing-mode branch returns the raw `fetch` Response object while every call site expects the provider's parsed token payload. With credential sharing enabled per the .env.example, GoogleCalendarService's `const token = res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError so Google refresh always fails; HubspotCalendarService assigns the Response to `HubspotToken` and computes `Date.now() + undefined * 1000` = NaN, persisting a garbage expiryDate to the credential; office365video/lark/zoom feed the sync endpoint's `{access_token, expiry}` body to handlers typed for Microsoft/Lark/Zoom response contracts and persist incomplete credentials.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` object in the sharing-mode branch (`if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId) { ... return response; }`). Multiple call sites shown in the diff expect provider/SDK/axios-style return shapes, not a `Response`: GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but a `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw. Similarly, zoho-bigin/zohocrm wrap `axios(...)` in `refreshOAuthTokens` and then access `.data`, which will be `undefined` if the function returned a `Response`. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable mismatch that will break token refresh when sharing mode is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Salesforce connection path now eagerly refreshes the token and overwrites `credential.key` on every service instantiation, and in sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse's minimum schema strips the Salesforce response down to `{access_token}`, so the persisted key becomes just `{access_token, refresh_token}`. Every Salesforce calendar operation now performs an extra OAuth roundtrip plus a credential write, and a transient refresh failure throws (HttpError / rejected connection promise) where the previous constructor proceeded on the stored access token, failing the whole operation; in sharing mode the overwrite permanently drops `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, and `token_type` from the stored credential, so the next instantiation builds the jsforce connection with an undefined instanceUrl and every subsequent Salesforce call fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token request immediately during service initialization (it `fetch`es the Salesforce token endpoint and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `jsforce.Connection`). This means every instantiation triggers an extra OAuth roundtrip and a DB write regardless of whether the stored access token is still valid, and a transient refresh failure now throws/rejects early (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`). Additionally, the refresh parsing path uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which in “sharing mode” (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set) validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) rather than the Salesforce schema, and because it’s a `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`, it will drop fields not declared in the minimum schema. The subsequent credential write persists only the parsed fields plus the old `refresh_token` (`data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }`), so important Salesforce fields like `instance_url` can be lost from `credential.key` if they are not part of the minimum schema, causing follow-on breakage wherever those fields are required.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook's update branch replaces `credential.key` wholesale with caller-supplied decrypted JSON (`data: { key: keys }`), with no validation against the app's credential schema and no merge with the existing key. A payload containing only the access token and expiry — the exact shape the sync flow documents — wipes the stored refresh_token and other schema-required fields, permanently bricking a working credential with no backup; the `findFirst` at lines 62-70 has no orderBy or type filter, so when a user has multiple credentials for the same app an arbitrary row is overwritten.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the update path does `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` where `keys` is caller-supplied decrypted JSON (`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`). There is no schema validation and no merge with the existing stored key, so any omitted fields (e.g., `refresh_token` or other required properties for that app’s credential shape) will be dropped, potentially breaking existing credentials. Additionally, the existing credential is selected via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` with no `orderBy` and no additional discriminator (e.g., type), so if multiple credential rows exist for the same `userId`+`appId`, an arbitrary one may be overwritten.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zoho-bigin refresh call passes `credentialId` (the credential row id) as the userId parameter that every other call site fills with `credential.userId`, so the sync request posts `calcomUserId=<credential id>`. With credential sharing enabled, the parent app resolves that value to a different or nonexistent user and returns that user's Zoho tokens — syncing another user's credentials into this user's credential row, or breaking the token mapping entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the third argument is treated as a Cal.com *userId* (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Google Calendar's token refresh stores the Zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse — an object of the shape {success: true, data: {...}} — as the credential key, instead of the parsed credentials that the replaced googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) returned. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (an envelope with `{ success, data, error? }`), not the parsed `data` itself (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, which returns `refreshTokenResponse`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed schema keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the constant string '[object Object]' (zod schemas have no custom toString) and collapse into one duplicate key, so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires only access_token and implements none of the intended expiry or refresh_token validation. In sync mode the schema accepts any response containing an access_token string while zod's default unknown-key stripping silently deletes every other field from the parsed data: office365-calendar keeps a stale expires_in and re-runs the refresh on every single calendar operation (a sync fetch plus a DB write per booking), and salesforce — whose own provider response is run through this branch too, because the branch keys only off the env flags — persists key = {access_token, refresh_token}, losing instance_url so the next operation builds its jsforce connection against an undefined instance URL and every Salesforce call fails, all while parse reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, minimumTokenResponseSchema defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In JS object literals, those computed keys are evaluated immediately to a string; for Zod schema objects this will be a constant (e.g., "[object Object]"), so the two entries collide and do not create a dynamic “any string key” shape. As a result, in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and strips all other fields, so token responses can be “successfully” parsed while losing important fields (e.g., Office365 token fields, Salesforce `instance_url`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the token response lacks refresh_token — exactly the shape the sync-mode contract prescribes ('the response should only contain the access token and expiry date') — the code writes the literal string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data, which callers spread into the credentials they persist. On the first sync-mode refresh, office365-calendar and zoomvideo overwrite the user's real refresh token with the string 'refresh_token' inside the credential row, with no error raised at overwrite time; any later direct provider refresh posts refresh_token=refresh_token and receives invalid_grant, permanently killing the integration (re-auth required) once the real token is gone.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` unconditionally injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the parsed token payload lacks a refresh token (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In sync mode the minimum schema intentionally allows responses without `refresh_token`, so this branch will run. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned data is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, which will overwrite the real stored refresh token with the literal string.
