adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and then JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)) with no try/catch, so a malformed body or a payload encrypted with a mismatched key throws out of the handler. The parent application receives a raw 500 (Next's unhandled route error) instead of the 4xx JSON every sibling branch of this endpoint returns, so it cannot distinguish a bad payload from a broken Cal.com deployment — retries loop on the 500 and integration debugging has no message to work with.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and then `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` without any try/catch. Both `parse` (throws on invalid input) and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` (can throw on wrong key, malformed ciphertext, or non-JSON plaintext) will raise unhandled exceptions, causing Next.js to return a generic 500 rather than the explicit 4xx JSON responses used in the other branches of this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SalesforceCalendarService now unconditionally refreshes the access token (a blocking POST to login.salesforce.com plus a credential DB write) during construction, before building the jsforce connection, on every service instantiation. Every Salesforce calendar operation (availability checks and booking create/update/delete each construct the service) gains a sequential remote round-trip and a DB write, multiplying refreshes several-fold per booking; and any transient token-endpoint failure — expired refresh token, Salesforce login throttling, network blip — aborts construction so ALL Salesforce operations fail even when the stored access token was still valid, where previously the connection was built from stored tokens and jsforce refreshed lazily only on demand.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then immediately `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (i.e., before any calendar operation actually needs a refreshed token). There is no conditional check on access token validity/expiry; the refresh happens unconditionally whenever this code path runs, and any non-OK response throws (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`), which would prevent constructing the connection even if the stored `access_token` might still be usable. This adds a blocking network round-trip and a DB write to every instantiation and makes transient refresh failures fatal for all Salesforce operations using this service.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is issued with no timeout or AbortSignal, yet it sits inline on the request path of every calendar and video operation once the feature is enabled. A hung or slow parent endpoint (mid-deploy restart, network partition) stalls each affected booking/calendar request for up to undici's default multi-minute header/body timeouts instead of failing fast, and concurrent requests pile up against the parent, degrading every booking that touches a synced app.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) conditionally calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` without any `AbortSignal`/timeout. This helper is wired into multiple calendar/video integrations’ token refresh paths (e.g., GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, Zoom VideoApiAdapter, Webex, Lark, Hubspot, Zoho, etc.), meaning a slow/hung parent endpoint can block those server-side operations when credential sync is enabled. This is a concrete resilience/performance concern grounded in the diff, though it’s not a deterministic “broken” behavior in normal operation, so it’s better classified as an important non-bug issue rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zoho-bigin refresh passes `credentialId` — not `credential.userId`, as every other call site in this diff does — as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, so the credential row id lands in the calcomUserId request field. In sync mode the parent application receives a credential id where the contract defines the user id, so it resolves the wrong user (or none) and either fails the sync or attaches the wrong account's credentials; because the value is non-null, the null-guard that routes team credentials to the direct refresh cannot catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is `userId` and, in sync mode, it is sent as `calcomUserId` (`userId.toString()`) to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Every other updated call site in the diff passes `credential.userId`, so this one will send a credential row id (or at least a non-user id) where a user id is expected, leading to incorrect/failed sync and bypassing the `userId` null-guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Success is checked via `response.statusText !== 'OK'` and failures are thrown as HttpError({statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText}) without ever reading the response body. A 5xx from Salesforce (login throttling, maintenance) surfaces to the booking API as statusCode 400 with the reason phrase as the message — an incoherent '400 Service Unavailable' — and the actual cause in Salesforce's error body (invalid_grant, expired refresh token, rate limit) is discarded, so an operator debugging a dead Salesforce integration sees a client-error label on a server failure with no diagnostic content.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh flow checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });` and then only reads `await response.json()` on the success path. This (1) misclassifies non-OK HTTP responses (including 5xx) as a 400 client error, and (2) discards the response body on failure, losing Salesforce error details (e.g., `invalid_grant`). The finding matches this diff-grounded behavior exactly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook's credential upsert is a findFirst-then-update/create sequence with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), no transaction, and no idempotency guard. Two overlapping deliveries of the same webhook (senders commonly retry while a slow first request is still in flight) both see no credential and both create one, leaving duplicate rows for the same user and app; findFirst then returns an arbitrary row, so the stale duplicate intermittently serves expired keys — users see intermittent auth failures with no error surfaced anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the credential write is implemented as a non-atomic `findFirst` followed by `update` or `create` (see `prisma.credential.findFirst(...)` then `prisma.credential.create(...)`). There is no transaction, no Prisma `upsert`, and no idempotency key/guard, so concurrent/retried webhook deliveries can race: both requests can observe “no credential” and attempt `create`, which can either (a) create duplicates if the DB schema does not enforce uniqueness, or (b) throw on a unique constraint if it does—either way causing broken behavior under common retry patterns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The secret lookup uses process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim while Node lowercases all incoming header names, and the failed lookup is reported as 'Invalid webhook secret'. A deployer who sets the header name with any uppercase character (e.g. 'Calcom-Webhook-Secret') receives a permanent 403 'Invalid webhook secret' for every sync call and debugs the secret value instead of the header-name casing; lowercasing the env read would remove the trap.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check indexes `req.headers` with `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` verbatim: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. Node/Next request headers are typically normalized to lowercase keys, so if an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` with any uppercase characters, the lookup can fail and always return 403 `Invalid webhook secret`. The `.env.example` comment says the header name "Should be in lowercase", so this is a configuration footgun rather than an unconditional defect, but the finding is grounded and actionable (e.g., lowercasing the env value before indexing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The hunk deletes the only code that logged Microsoft's error body and the zod error detail for failed Office365 refreshes, and the new parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces the old log-and-continue behavior with a hard throw of a generic message. A refresh whose response no longer matches the schema (Microsoft response drift, invalid_grant) now both fails the refresh — taking down the operation that can no longer obtain a fresh token where it previously limped along on its still-valid stored token — and surfaces only 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'; the field-level cause and the Microsoft error body are discarded, removing the primary diagnostic for broken Office365 auth.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous behavior on Zod parse failure was to `console.error(...)` with both the Zod error and the Microsoft `responseJson`, then continue by updating Prisma with the (unchanged) `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`). The new code replaces `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly `throw`s `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails, while also removing the detailed logging. This is a real, diff-grounded regression in diagnosability and a behavior change from log-and-continue to fail-fast, though whether the stricter failure is a "bug" vs intentional is not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The example states the key 'must be 32 bytes for AES256' and then tells the operator to generate it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 bytes — while the sibling CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET line correctly uses `rand -base64 32`. A self-hoster following the example deploys a 24-byte key against a comment demanding 32: if symmetricDecrypt passes the key raw to an aes-256 createDecipheriv, every webhook decryption throws and the endpoint 500s on every call, bricking the sync integration at setup; under any key-normalizing implementation the 'must be 32 bytes' instruction is instead the false one — the two adjacent shipped lines cannot both be right.

adjudication.rationale: In `.env.example`, the new `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` guidance is internally inconsistent: it says the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256" but suggests generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24` (24 bytes of random data). The adjacent `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` correctly suggests `rand -base64 32`, reinforcing that `24` is likely a mistake. Since the runtime code (`symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`) depends on this key, a misleading example can lead to a broken setup for self-hosters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When the app row exists in the database but is absent from the app store metadata, the endpoint returns 404 'App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug'. The operator debugging a failed sync is told the slug is wrong when it demonstrably resolved (the row was found by the previous query) — the message names the wrong state and sends them hunting for typos instead of the real cause: the app is not present or enabled in this Cal.com build.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler first verifies the app exists in DB via `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })`. If that succeeds but `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is missing, it returns `404` with message `"App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"`. That message is misleading because the slug already matched an existing DB row; the actual failure is that the app is not present in `appStoreMetadata` for this build (e.g., app not included/enabled). This is a concrete, diff-grounded operator/debuggability issue, not a functional defect.
